text:
maya: Quick proposal — introduce a "dual-serve" canary pattern for long-tail catalog migrations. TL;DR: for low-volume models we route a small fraction to the new model while keeping the pinned model as primary for ~14 days, run a golden-prompt eval every 6 hours, and require both quality + perf gates before full cutover.

alex: thinking: this could reduce sudden regressions for customers who rely on quirks. what are the exact gates/thresholds?

jorge: rough thresholds to start the convo: acceptability delta >= -0.02 (i.e. no more than 2% drop), hallucination rate delta <= +1%, latency p95 delta <= +150ms. if any fail -> auto rollback to pinned. metrics computed on golden prompt set + sampled live traffic.

maya: +1. Also we should stop billing double for the overlapping requests — billing should attribute to the primary model; only charge extra if new-model response used for downstream tasks. @sasha can you confirm viability?

sasha: billing note: we can implement attribution via response tag in router. small infra change but doable. might take ~2 days to add meter-exception flag to router logs.

alex: infra questions — routing split plan? do we do fixed splits or ramping?

jorge: prefer ramped splits: 5% new / 95% pinned for 48h -> 25% / 75% for 48h -> 50/50 for 48h -> then evaluate and either flip or continue. duration paramizable per-catalog-entry.

maya: sounds reasonable. need to capture rollout metadata for audit (who started, why, duration, customer opt-outs). also plan for customer-facing comms if a visible change.

deploy-bot: deploy created: canary/dual-serve-1723456789 - config pending.

maya: example config (proto):
```
canary:
  id: dual-serve-1723456789
  duration_days: 14
  ramp_schedule: [ {hours:48, split:5}, {hours:48, split:25}, {hours:48, split:50} ]
  golden_eval_interval_hours: 6
  metrics:
    - name: acceptability_rate
      pass_if: delta >= -0.02
    - name: hallucination_rate
      pass_if: delta <= 0.01
    - name: p95_latency_ms
      pass_if: delta <= 150
  billing_attribution: primary_only
  customer_opt_out: true
```

alex: need to confirm the persistent KV for golden prompts + a webhook to feed eval results to the runbook. I'll add an endpoint on the eval service.

jorge: i'll own the orchestration & analysis (set up dashboards, synthetic vs live split). plan to surface a simple pass/fail badge per canary + time series for the three metrics.

maya: owner/next steps: jorge = owner for the canary run + dashboards, alex = infra changes (router attribution & eval webhook), sasha = billing flag and audit schema, maya = comms + acceptance criteria doc. target: prototype canary in staging by end of next week.

jorge: tentative rollback criteria: any metric breach sustained for 2 evaluation windows OR a customer-visible error spike (>0.1% error rate).

alex: +1 on rollout automation — add a kill-switch API so SRE can immediately roll back with one call.

maya: agreed. can we get a short README for the pattern (owner, expected time, how to opt-out, billing details)? i'll draft and circulate.

sasha: FYI — for customers on dedicated plans we should surface an opt-in flag in console rather than auto apply.

maya: noted. ok team — if no major objections i'll open a PR with the canary spec + sample config and tag owners. :thumbsup:

alex: 👍

jorge: 👍 I'll start dashboards and add the golden prompt set.

sasha: will queue billing work.

maya: thanks everyone — moving to action items.
